rows.name: switch-topic
rows.question: Switch topics. Why does snapshot isolation permit write skew even if both read-check-write sequences run in atomic transactions?
rows.recognizedQuestion: Switch topics. Why does snapshot isolation permit write skew even if both read-check-write sequences run in atomic transactions?
rows.answer:
Snapshot isolation makes each transaction atomic, but it does not make concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one at a time. Each transaction checks its own consistent snapshot, and ordinary snapshot isolation detects conflicting writes to the same row—not every conflict between what one transaction reads and another writes.

For example, suppose Alice and Bob are both on call, and the rule is that at least one must remain on call. Two concurrent transactions each read that both are on call; one then marks Alice off call, while the other marks Bob off call. Because they update different rows, both can commit, leaving nobody on call even though each check passed.

Atomicity guarantees that each transaction’s changes happen entirely or not at all; it does not guarantee that its check remains valid against concurrent changes. Preventing this write skew requires serializable isolation or an explicit locking or shared-write scheme that forces these transactions to conflict.
rows.usefulPrefix: Snapshot isolation makes each transaction atomic, but it does not make concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one at a time.
